sources.citation: Aron, A., Melinat, E., Aron, E. N., Vallone, R. D., & Bator, R. J. (1997). The experimental generation of interpersonal closeness: A procedure and some preliminary findings. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 23(4), 363-377.
sources.used_for: Sustained, escalating, reciprocal self-disclosure builds closeness; the bank climbs from depth 1 to depth 3 and agents take turns.

sources.citation: Kardas, M., Kumar, A., & Epley, N. (2022). Overly shallow?: Miscalibrated expectations create a barrier to deeper conversation. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 122(3), 367-398 (online first 2021).
sources.used_for: People overestimate how awkward deep talk will be and underestimate how connected it makes them feel; the bank reserves about 20% for deep questions.

sources.citation: Alves, H. (2018). Sharing rare attitudes attracts. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 44(8), 1270-1283.
sources.used_for: Overlap on uncommon attitudes and interests produces more attraction than overlap on common ones; many questions ask for the niche, specific thing ('rare').

sources.citation: Montoya, R. M., Horton, R. S., & Kirchner, J. (2008). Is actual similarity necessary for attraction? A meta-analysis of actual and perceived similarity. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 25(6), 889-922.
sources.used_for: Perceived similarity predicts attraction in real interactions, so questions ask for named specifics (the exact game, bug, or band), never a category.

sources.citation: Hall, J. A. (2019). How many hours does it take to make a friend? Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 36(4), 1278-1296.
sources.used_for: Friendship takes repeated contact (roughly 50 hours to casual friend), so future_and_followup questions surface reasons and times to meet again.

sources.citation: Huang, K., Yeomans, M., Brooks, A. W., Minson, J., & Gino, F. (2017). It doesn't hurt to ask: Question-asking increases liking. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 113(3), 430-452.
sources.used_for: Follow-up questions in particular increase liking; followup_ok marks questions that build on the previous answer.

sources.citation: Sprecher, S., Treger, S., Wondra, J. D., Hilaire, N., & Wallpe, K. (2013). Taking turns: Reciprocal self-disclosure promotes liking in initial interactions. Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, 49(5), 860-866.
sources.used_for: Back-and-forth disclosure beats one-sided disclosure; agents alternate asking and answering.

sources.citation: Festinger, L., Schachter, S., & Back, K. (1950). Social Pressures in Informal Groups: A Study of Human Factors in Housing. Harper.
sources.used_for: Proximity and easy chances to interact drive tie formation; now_at_hackgt questions find a reason to talk during the event ('soon').

sources.citation: Rajkumar, K., Saint-Jacques, G., Bojinov, I., Brynjolfsson, E., & Aral, S. (2022). A causal test of the strength of weak ties. Science, 377(6612), 1304-1310.
sources.used_for: Moderately weak ties carry outsized career value; career and stuck/solved questions look for mutual value (one can fix what the other is stuck on).

types.now_at_hackgt: What the human is building, needing, and feeling at HackGT 13 right now: a reason to talk during the event.
types.building_and_craft: How the human builds: tools, stacks, taste, and the specific things they have made.
types.stuck_and_solved: Problems the human is stuck on and problems they have already solved, to find who can unblock whom.
types.career_and_path: Where the human's work and studies are heading, and what help or experience they can trade.
types.where_from: The human's origins: how they grew up, got into making things, and got here.
types.interests_and_rare: Specific, niche interests outside work, where rare overlap sparks the strongest connection.
types.values_and_beliefs: What the human believes, cares about, and will not compromise on.
types.life_and_personal: The human's life outside the hackathon: routines, what they are going through, and who matters to them.
types.fun_and_play: Playful, low-stakes questions that get both humans laughing.
types.future_and_followup: Follow-ups that deepen the last answer, plus reasons and times to meet again after HackGT.
